kings.name: Shamshi-Adad I
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Amorite conqueror who took Assur and built the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia, ruling from Shubat-Enlil.
kings.source: Old Assyrian royal inscriptions; Mari archives

kings.name: Gungunum
kings.title: King of Larsa
kings.description: King of Larsa who broke free of Isin and briefly held Ur.

kings.name: Rim-Sin I
kings.title: King of Larsa
kings.description: Last great king of Larsa; conquered Isin before being overthrown by Hammurabi.

kings.name: Zimri-Lim
kings.title: King of Mari
kings.description: Last king of Mari, famed through the Mari archives; conquered by Hammurabi of Babylon.

kings.name: Samsu-iluna
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: Son of Hammurabi whose reign saw the loss of the south to the First Sealand Dynasty.
kings.source: Samsu-iluna year names; Babylonian king list

kings.name: Iluma-ilum
kings.title: King of the Sealand
kings.description: Founder of the First Sealand Dynasty, which broke the south away from Babylon.

kings.name: Samsu-ditana
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: Last king of the First Dynasty of Babylon, overthrown when the Hittites sacked the city.

kings.name: Mursili I
kings.title: King of the Hittites
kings.description: Hittite king who raided down the Euphrates and sacked Babylon, ending its First Dynasty.

kings.name: Agum II
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: Kassite ruler who restored Babylon and returned the statue of Marduk after the Hittite sack.

kings.name: Burnaburiash II
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: Kassite king of Babylon whose diplomatic correspondence survives in the Amarna letters.

kings.name: Adad-nirari I
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Assyrian king who conquered Mitanni and turned Assyria into a great power.

kings.name: Tukulti-Ninurta I
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Assyrian king who defeated the Kassites and sacked Babylon, carrying off the statue of Marduk.

kings.name: Tiglath-Pileser I
kings.title: King of Assyria
kings.description: Middle Assyrian king who campaigned to the Mediterranean and against Babylon.

kings.name: Shutruk-Nakhunte
kings.title: King of Elam
kings.description: Elamite king who sacked Babylonia and carried the Code of Hammurabi stele to Susa.

kings.name: Nebuchadnezzar I
kings.title: King of Babylon
kings.description: King of the Second Dynasty of Isin who defeated Elam and recovered the statue of Marduk.

events.name: The Destruction of the Kanesh Merchant Colony
events.description: The Old Assyrian merchant colony (karum) at Kanesh is destroyed in a conflagration, preserving thousands of clay tablets.

events.name: Shamshi-Adad I Conquers Assur
events.description: Shamshi-Adad I seizes Assur and proclaims himself king, founding the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia.
events.source: Old Assyrian royal inscriptions; Mari archives

events.name: Gungunum of Larsa Takes Ur
events.description: Gungunum wrests Ur from Isin and extends Larsa's power over the south.

events.name: Rim-Sin I Conquers Isin
events.description: Rim-Sin of Larsa captures Isin, ending the Dynasty of Isin and leaving Larsa the dominant southern state.

events.name: Hammurabi Conquers Larsa
events.description: Hammurabi of Babylon defeats Rim-Sin and annexes Larsa, uniting the whole of Sumer and Akkad under Babylon.

events.name: Hammurabi Conquers Mari
events.description: Hammurabi sacks Mari and brings down Zimri-Lim, ending the Mari kingdom whose archives chronicle the age.

events.name: Hammurabi Defeats Eshnunna
events.description: Hammurabi takes Eshnunna and its territories in the Diyala region, completing Babylon's dominance.

events.name: The Code of Hammurabi
events.description: Hammurabi promulgates his law code, the most complete legal monument of the ancient Near East.

events.name: Samsu-iluna Loses the South
events.description: Revolts in the south under Samsu-iluna end with Iluma-ilum founding the First Sealand Dynasty, splitting Babylonia.
events.source: Samsu-iluna year names; Babylonian king list

events.name: The Hittite Sack of Babylon
events.description: Mursili I of the Hittites sacks Babylon and deposes Samsu-ditana, ending the First Dynasty of Babylon.

events.name: Agum II Restores Marduk to Babylon
events.description: The Kassite Agum II recovers the statue of Marduk from the land of Hana and restores Babylon.

events.name: Burnaburiash II Corresponds with Egypt
events.description: Kassite king Burnaburiash II exchanges royal letters with the pharaohs, preserved in the Amarna archive.

events.name: Adad-nirari I Conquers Mitanni
events.description: Adad-nirari I overruns what remained of Mitanni and annexes its heartland, making Assyria a great power.

events.name: Tukulti-Ninurta I Sacks Babylon
events.description: Tukulti-Ninurta I defeats Kashtiliash IV and sacks Babylon, carrying the statue of Marduk back to Assur.

events.name: Tiglath-Pileser I Campaigns to the Mediterranean
events.description: Tiglath-Pileser I campaigns across northern Syria to the Mediterranean and receives tribute from Byblos.

events.name: Shutruk-Nakhunte Sacks Babylonia
events.description: The Elamite king Shutruk-Nakhunte sacks Babylonian cities and carries trophies including the Code of Hammurabi stele to Susa.

events.name: Nebuchadnezzar I Defeats Elam
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar I routs the Elamites and recovers the statue of Marduk, restoring Babylonian pride.
